c: CROWN

Headpiece symbolizing honor or high office. In addition to using the word metaphorically, the OT refers to three kinds of crowns. One type of crown was worn by the high priest and Hebrew kings. The high priest’s “holy crown” was a gold plate engraved with the words “Holy to the Lord” fastened to the front of a turban (
). It symbolized his consecration as the people’s representative before God. The Hebrew kings wore a crown light enough to be worn into battle (
)—perhaps a narrow band of silk studded with jewels. Like the high priest’s, the king’s crown also indicated a divinely appointed office (
). A second type of crown was a massive gold and jeweled symbol of office worn by pagan kings and idols (
). The prophet Zechariah placed such a crown on Joshua the high priest to indicate the union of royal and priestly functions (
). A third type of crown was a wreath of flowers used at a banquet to symbolize joy and celebration (
